dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Nam, can I ask you some more questions about Thai manners?
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, kən aɪ ˈæsk juː sʌm ˈmɔːr ˈkwɛstʃənz əˈbaʊt ˈtaɪ ˈmænərz?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: In Canada, it's fine to touch a child's head. Is that OK in Thailand?
dialogue.reading: ɪn ˈkænədə, ɪts ˈfaɪn tə ˈtʌtʃ ə ˈtʃaɪldz ˈhɛd. ɪz ðæt oʊˈkeɪ ɪn ˈtaɪlænd?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: No. The head is considered special, so it's considered impolite to touch someone's head.
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ. ðə ˈhɛd ɪz kənˈsɪdərd ˈspɛʃəl, soʊ ɪts kənˈsɪdərd ˌɪmpəˈlaɪt tə ˈtʌtʃ ˈsʌmwʌnz ˈhɛd.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Oh! I didn't know that. What about feet?
dialogue.reading: ˈoʊ! aɪ ˈdɪdənt ˈnoʊ ˈðæt. ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ˈfiːt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Feet are considered dirty. It's considered rude to point at people or things with your feet.
dialogue.reading: ˈfiːt ər kənˈsɪdərd ˈdɜːrti. ɪts kənˈsɪdərd ˈruːd tə ˈpɔɪnt ət ˈpiːpəl ɔːr ˈθɪŋz wɪð jʊr ˈfiːt.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: OK. Can I point at things with my finger?
dialogue.reading: oʊˈkeɪ. kən aɪ ˈpɔɪnt ət ˈθɪŋz wɪð maɪ ˈfɪŋɡər?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: It's more polite to use your hand, not one finger.
dialogue.reading: ɪts ˈmɔːr pəˈlaɪt tə ˈjuːz jʊr ˈhænd, ˈnɑːt ˈwʌn ˈfɪŋɡər.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: And is it rude to whistle in the house? I sometimes whistle when I cook.
dialogue.reading: ənd ɪz ɪt ˈruːd tə ˈwɪsəl ɪn ðə ˈhaʊs? aɪ ˈsʌmtaɪmz ˈwɪsəl wɛn aɪ ˈkʊk.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Some older Thais say that whistling at night brings bad luck.
dialogue.reading: sʌm ˈoʊldər ˈtaɪz ˈseɪ ðæt ˈwɪsəlɪŋ ət ˈnaɪt ˈbrɪŋz ˈbæd ˈlʌk.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Really? I don't want to offend your aunt!
dialogue.reading: ˈriːli? aɪ ˈdoʊnt ˈwɑːnt tə əˈfɛnd jʊr ˈænt!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Don't worry. She knows you're from Canada. She won't be offended.
dialogue.reading: ˈdoʊnt ˈwɜːri. ʃiː ˈnoʊz jʊr frəm ˈkænədə. ʃiː ˈwoʊnt bi əˈfɛndɪd.
